We ran into some questions in the PBF that don't have clear answers at all.  I'm hoping a developer can chime in here.

  • When a character uses an ability that has multiple effects that trigger off different dice, like Tachyon's Hypersonic Assault, and also has a Boost or a Hinder, does the modifier apply to all dice/effects, just one of their choice, just the first one described in the ability, or what?
  • Do Boosts and Hinders apply to Minion Saves?
  • If they do apply to minion saves, and an ability like Quick Insight both applies a Hinder to a target and then attacks it, does the Hinder immediately apply to that save?
  • When a roll is modified by a Boost or Hinder and also triggers a Twist based on the roll, are the effects of the Twist also modified?

Edit: Oh, and a Unity-specific question:

  • "Volatile Parts" triggers on "one of your bonuses, penalties, or minions is destroyed."  This is clear for minions, but I'm assuming that "destroyed" specifically means by other abilities that say "destroy" and not being consumed or canceled by an opposite penalty or bonus.  But what does "your" mean?  Usually "your" bonus means a bonus you have available for yourself, but that doesn't make sense in this context.  I'm guessing it means "bonus or penalty you created," but I'd like to see that officially stated.

Because only they know the intent of the rules, and not just what's on the pages.  I know a lot of people know the rules as written very well, but I also know that this happens a lot:

  • Someone plays several games with the developers and feels like they know the rules, despite certain situations never coming up.
  • Someone then plays games with these "tier-2" GM's and then feel like they know the rules, but some of them are wrong.
  • Someone plays games with these "tier 3" GM's and feel like they know the rules, and answer them, but are now quite wrong.
And here is a perfect example: Paul says that Hinders always apply on the very next roll.  Dave says that Hinders apply when the character who created it says so (declared before the roll).  One of them is wrong, and I'm guessing it's the one who didn't develop the game (Paul--who I would otherwise ordinarily consider a very high authority).

If something isn't explicitly written in the rulebook, I want clarification from an authoritative source before considering it correct.  Otherwise, I can read the rules as well as anyone else.

posts.cooked:
MindWanderer:
Whoa... that's very different from the way I've seen it played in any game so far.  It affects one  die , not the outcome?  So if you're Hindered -3 during Hypersonic Assault and roll 10, 5, 2, you can apply the Hinder effect to the 10--effectively taking no penalty at all?  That's huge, and really weakens the power of Hinders used on the heroes.

Not sure we're talking about the same thing then. Whoever made the bonus/penalty chooses what it applies to, as also defined by what the bonus or penalty actually is in the game world. It's applied to one effect die - a bonus or penalty isn't ever going to be used on a non-effect die. See page 9 of the gameplay guide.

However, if you have a bonus that you use on an attack that affects multiple targets with your Min die, that bonus is only applying to that die, so the damage to each is increased accordingly. 

Say you're taking the "lose health equal to the Max die" twist and you used a boost on a "Principle of X" ability (and thus, you boosted the Max die).  Do you take more damage?

Ah, I see. Largely this would be the GM's call based on what the boost was and how the twist was created because they're the one choosing the twist, though in general, I'd say losing health equal to Max die from a twist isn't an effect die and so mods don't really apply.
